page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No marginal notes. Printed page number "59" at the head, centred. Gathering signature "D 4" at the foot, right of centre. Left-edge fragments belong to the neighbouring page and are left out.

main_text.p: que Philosophus quisquam est, neque Iurisconsultus, qui neget ei paratam esse excusationem legitimam non parendi, qui omnino non parere non potest ideo quia omni ad parendum facultate pri-vatus est.
Habet ergo homo facultatem ali-quam, mentem nempe atque voluntatem, sed ad quam aliquid accessit quod eius operationem impedit atque inter-cipit.

Impedimentum illud non potest in ulla alia re situm esse praeterquam in certa quadam constitutione facultatis. Constitutio autem talis nulla est nisi quae vel intelligendi atque ratiocinandi vim aufert ex intellectu, vel ratiocinandi quidem atque intelligendi vim in homine relinquit, at facit tamen ut non bene iudicet de scopo ad quem actiones suas referre debet, & nequeat, ut loquitur Aristoteles, ὀρθοδοξεῖν πρὸς τὸ τέλος[?].

Prioris generis impedimentum aequipollet omnimodae privationi facultatis. Haud enim minus excusatur vel infans in quo ὁ λογικὸν[?] est non ἀπλῶς modo, sed ex organorum imperfectione praepedi-tum, vel adultus, qui casu aliquo factus

page.notes: The Greek phrases on the last lines of the page are small and partly blurred. ὀρθοδοξεῖν πρὸς τὸ τέλος and ὁ λογικὸν are my best reading; the accents and breathings are uncertain, so they are marked [?]. The Greek ἀπλῶς is read with reasonable confidence. Long s was normalised to s throughout, per the house rules (e.g. "eft" as "est", "Conftitutio" as "Constitutio"). The u/v spelling was normalised (e.g. "priuatus" as "privatus", "vt" as "ut"). No printing errors were identified.
